title: Schema-aware partial-object stitching and idempotent retry contract for streaming structured outputs
creator: Priya Patel
description: Problem: When clients consume streaming model outputs as application-level JSON objects, truncation, backpressure, or connection resets commonly produce partial JSON objects (cut strings, missing closing brackets, incomplete arrays). This leads to two classes of failure: (1) consumers drop partially-built application state because parsing fails, and (2) retries produce duplicated side-effects when tool/function calls are repeated without idempotency, or cause inconsistency when the model produces a different continuation on retry. Goal: Define and implement a schema-aware "partial-object stitching" and idempotent retry contract that lets clients and servers recover or safely retry streaming structured outputs without requiring a full protocol overhaul or breaking older clients. Non-goals: This ticket does not rework transport-level guarantees (we assume best-effort streaming) and does not implement persistent server-side per-request state beyond lightweight checkpoints and immutable idempotency tokens.
design:
Overview: Add lightweight markers and a compatibility layer so:
  1) Model runtime can emit optional chunk-level envelopes with three metadata fields: "checkpoint_id", "schema_anchor", and "call_anchor". These are NOT required for clients that only read raw bytes. 2) Clients that understand the contract can treat partial JSON fragments as candidates for stitching if they share a checkpoint_id and schema_anchor. The server maintains an ephemeral immutable replay buffer of prefix tokens for in-flight requests for a bounded TTL (default 30s) keyed by idempotency token. 3) On connection loss or explicit retry, the client requests a replay from the server using the idempotency token and the last successfully-applied schema path (e.g., /items/4/title). The server responds with a minimal prefix that leads to a valid continuation or returns a canonical "replay-not-possible" error. 4) Tool/function calls are annotated with call_anchor and a generated call_id; the client can map call_ids to external side-effects and apply at-most-once semantics by either deduplicating downstream or routing retries to a benign fallback variant.

Key protocol pieces:
- Envelopes: JSON-lines metadata ahead of a chunk: {"checkpoint_id":"hex","schema_anchor":"/users/2/addresses/0","call_anchor":"call-83d"}. Consumers that do not parse envelopes ignore them. - Schema anchors: path-like pointers into the declared output schema (or best-effort guessed path) that indicate the location the upcoming fragment is populating. - Checkpoints: opaque tokens the server can later use to produce a deterministic prefix for safe replay. - Idempotency token: required for any request that triggers external tool calls; provided by client in header X-Idempotency-Token. - Replay API: POST /v1/replay with body {"idempotency_token":"...","last_applied_anchor":"...","max_prefix_tokens":2000}. Server returns either a prefix stream or error.

Compatibility strategy: If server emits envelopes but client ignores them, behavior is unchanged: client receives raw stream bytes. New clients gain stronger recovery. For older servers, clients fall back to conservative truncation heuristics and local repair using the schema. For tool calls, if the server lacks call_anchor support, clients must provide their own call deduplication (recommended via a call_id header) and maintain local retry policies.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Unit tests for envelope parsing, anchor matching, and local stitch algorithm. 2) Integration test: simulate truncation at 5 different offsets and validate consumer reconstructs valid JSON for 95% of cases in synthetic schema corpus. 3) End-to-end test for tool-calls: simulate a network interruption during a tool call and verify downstream side-effects are deduplicated when X-Idempotency-Token is used. 4) Backwards-compatibility smoke test: clients that ignore envelopes still receive identical raw bytes. 5) Performance: adding envelopes increases median tail latency by <0.5ms and memory overhead per request <2MB for the replay buffer under 99th percentile load.
testing_plan:
- Unit: envelope encoder/decoder, schema_anchor resolver, partial-object zipper.
- Fuzz: generate random truncation offsets across ~200 declared schemas (flat, nested arrays, optional fields) and assert stitched JSON matches full-run output when possible.
- Load: run 5000 concurrent streaming requests with envelopes enabled to measure CPU and memory impact and verify replay TTL rolloffs.
- Chaos: drop TCP mid-chunk and verify client replay requests either get a valid prefix or a non-replay error with clear remediation guidance.
- Tool-call: assert call_id and X-Idempotency-Token dedupe logic in a sandboxed webhook receiver.
- Observability: add metrics streaming.stitch.success_rate, streaming.replay.requests, streaming.replay.failures, streaming.call.deduped.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature-flag the envelope emission and replay buffer on runtime (FF-streaming-envelopes).
2) Deploy to internal canary for 48h and run synthetic truncation test.
3) Gradually enable for 10% of hosted traffic with server-side replay buffer limit of 5s TTL.
4) Expand to 50% with 30s TTL and increased buffer sizing.
5) Enable 100% after 2 weeks of stable metrics.
6) Post-mortem and doc updates.
api_changes: - New optional response-envelopes emitted as ldjson metadata lines. - New client header X-Idempotency-Token (recommended for any tool-call requests). - New replay endpoint POST /v1/replay. - New field in streaming telemetry: envelope_present=true/false. - All changes are additive; no breaking changes to existing endpoints.
open_risks_and_tradeoffs: - Server-side replay buffer increases memory usage; tradeoff between TTL and likelihood of successful replay. We limit default TTL and allow admin tuning. - If a model produces a non-deterministic continuation, replayed prefix may not match original continuation; we mitigate by documenting regression windows and preferring deterministic seeds on idempotency-enabled requests. - Relying on schema anchors requires a decent schema or robust heuristic; brittle schemas will reduce stitch success rate. - Tool-call deduplication requires clients to adopt idempotency tokens; we will provide SDK helpers, but adoption may lag.

Runtime: implement envelope emission and lightweight in-memory prefix buffer
API: implement /v1/replay endpoint and X-Idempotency-Token validation
SDK: add helpers for idempotency tokens and envelope parsing in Python/TS
Docs: update streaming protocol docs and migration guide
Observability: add metrics and traces for stitch/replay flows
Rollout: implement FF and emergency disable path
updates: 2026-03-02: Created ticket after customer incident where streamed order objects were lost mid-stream during an outage. Collected logs and example traces.
2026-03-04: Spike complete. Proved small replay buffer + schema-anchor heuristics can repair ~78% of synthetic truncations for our corpus. Performance impact minimal at low concurrency.
2026-03-08: Design review with Runtime and SDK teams. Agreed on envelope ldjson format and X-Idempotency-Token header. Decided replay TTL default 30s.
2026-03-10: PR opened: runtime:streaming-envelopes (#4823). Basic envelope emission and parsing tests included. Blocked on replay API auth semantics discussion.
2026-03-12: Implemented SDK helper for generating stable idempotency tokens and call_id mapping (python-sdk pr #829). Running integration tests in CI.
2026-03-13: Integration tests show stitch success rate 92% for conservative heuristic; increasing schema-aware resolver precision under investigation. Moving to canary deploy by end of week.
notes_for_release: Document the new headers and replay endpoint in runtime-1.20 release notes. Add migration guide for SDKs and a checklist for customers using tool-calls to adopt X-Idempotency-Token. Provide an opt-out flag for sensitive workloads that cannot retain even ephemeral replay buffers.
